---

# 1. Load & Prepare Data

Two changes versus the original `load_cs()`:

1. **Contiguous integer period index.** The original coded `period` as
   `YYYY*100 + MM` (e.g. 202012, 202101). `aggte(type = "dynamic")` computes
   event time as `e = t - g` from the *raw* `tname`/`gname` values, so across a
   year boundary that difference is 89, not 1. The `type = "simple"`
   aggregation that feeds the headline table is unaffected (it only needs the
   post/pre ordering), but the dynamic event-study plots and the
   `min_e`/`max_e` windows are distorted. Coding `period` as a dense rank
   (1, 2, 3, ...) makes both aggregations correct regardless of `did` version.

2. **Quarterly aggregation.** When `TIME_UNIT == "quarter"`, raw monthly
   counts are summed within firm-quarter *before* the `log1p`, and `g` is
   floored to the quarter that contains the approval date. Aggregating the
   counts and then logging (rather than averaging monthly logs) is the
   correct order for an additive count outcome.

```{r time-helpers}
# Floor a Date to the start of its time unit
floor_unit <- function(d, unit = TIME_UNIT) {
  if (unit == "month") {
    as.Date(format(d, "%Y-%m-01"))
  } else {  # quarter
    q  <- (as.integer(format(d, "%m")) - 1L) %/% 3L          # 0..3
    mm <- sprintf("%02d", q * 3L + 1L)                       # 01,04,07,10
    as.Date(paste0(format(d, "%Y"), "-", mm, "-01"))
  }
}

# All n_collabs* columns are outcome counts; everything else is meta/covariate
count_cols <- function(df) grep("^n_collabs", names(df), value = TRUE)
```

```{r load-data}
load_cs <- function(path, unit = TIME_UNIT) {
  df <- read.csv(path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  df$month <- as.Date(df$month)

  ccols <- count_cols(df)

  # Covariates that are constant within firm (carried through aggregation)
  firm_cov <- c("g", "is_treated", "is_control", "matched_to",
                "nace1_psm", "nace1_proxy", "firm_type",
                "log_staffCount", "age",
                "log_collab_count_2020", "degree_centrality_2020")
  firm_cov <- intersect(firm_cov, names(df))

  # ── Collapse to the chosen time unit ───────────────────────────────────────
  df$tunit <- floor_unit(df$month, unit)

  # Level outcomes (per-month means, e.g. consortium size) are AVERAGED within
  # firm-quarter, NOT summed like the counts. (Absent in old panels -> no-op.)
  level_cols <- intersect(c("mean_collab_size", "mean_collab_size_active"), names(df))

  if (unit == "quarter") {
    counts <- df %>%
      group_by(Linkedin_name, tunit) %>%
      summarise(across(all_of(ccols), ~ sum(.x, na.rm = TRUE)),
                .groups = "drop")
    meta <- df %>%
      group_by(Linkedin_name) %>%
      summarise(across(all_of(firm_cov), ~ dplyr::first(.x)),
                .groups = "drop")
    levels_q <- if (length(level_cols)) df %>%
      group_by(Linkedin_name, tunit) %>%
      summarise(across(all_of(level_cols), ~ mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE)),  # AVERAGE, not sum
                .groups = "drop") else NULL
    df <- counts %>% left_join(meta, by = "Linkedin_name")
    if (!is.null(levels_q)) df <- df %>% left_join(levels_q, by = c("Linkedin_name", "tunit"))
  } else {
    # monthly: tunit == month, nothing to sum, just keep one row per firm-month
    # (.keep_all carries mean_collab_size through unchanged)
    df <- df %>% distinct(Linkedin_name, tunit, .keep_all = TRUE)
  }

  # ── Contiguous integer period index (1..T) ─────────────────────────────────
  u_periods   <- sort(unique(df$tunit))
  period_idx  <- setNames(seq_along(u_periods), as.character(u_periods))
  df$period   <- as.integer(period_idx[as.character(df$tunit)])

  # ── g_period on the same contiguous scale (0 = never-treated) ───────────────
  df$g <- as.character(df$g)
  df$g[df$g == "" | df$g == "NA"] <- NA
  g_unit <- floor_unit(as.Date(df$g), unit)
  df$g_period <- period_idx[as.character(g_unit)]
  df$g_period[is.na(df$g_period)] <- 0L
  df$g_period <- as.numeric(df$g_period)

  df$firm_id <- as.integer(factor(df$Linkedin_name))

  # ── log1p every count column generically -> log_<name> ─────────────────────
  for (cc in ccols) {
    df[[sub("^n_collabs", "log_collabs", cc)]] <- log1p(df[[cc]])
  }

  # ── extensive-margin (binary) version of every count column ────────────────
  for (cc in ccols) {
    df[[sub("^n_collabs", "any_collabs", cc)]] <- as.integer(df[[cc]] > 0)
  }

  # ── difference-of-logs contrasts (mirrors _cs_helpers.R::load_cs) ──────────
  # Built here so the inline PSM loader and the shared helper stay identical.
  # They are NOT added to outcome_map below, so they never enter att_table or
  # its Benjamini-Hochberg family; they are estimated as secondary analyses in
  # 10_ck_diagnostics_reference_country.R and reported with nominal p-values.
  for (tech in c("battery", "hydrogen")) {
    f <- paste0("log_collabs_", tech)
    u <- paste0("log_collabs_nonfunded_", tech)
    if (all(c(f, u) %in% names(df)))
      df[[paste0("log_rel_tech_", tech)]] <- df[[f]] - df[[u]]
    # Geographic contrast on the COLLABORATION-LEVEL, mutually exclusive
    # categories. The earlier version differenced the dyad-level cross-border EU
    # and non-EU outcomes, which overlap (one collaboration could enter both),
    # so that contrast was attenuated by construction and is not used.
    e <- paste0("log_collabs_eu_internal_", tech)
    n <- paste0("log_collabs_international_", tech)
    if (all(c(e, n) %in% names(df)))
      df[[paste0("log_rel_geo_", tech)]] <- df[[e]] - df[[n]]
  }

  df
}

battery_s1  <- load_cs(PATH_BATTERY_S1)
hydrogen_s1 <- load_cs(PATH_HYDROGEN_S1)
battery_s2  <- load_cs(PATH_BATTERY_S2)
hydrogen_s2 <- load_cs(PATH_HYDROGEN_S2)

# ROBUSTNESS = larger-control-group power spec (spec2: battery_s2, hydrogen_s2).
```

```{r outcome-map}
# ============================================================
# Outcome map: which column each technology uses.
# ============================================================
#
#   label                     battery column                 hydrogen column
#   ------------------------  -----------------------------  ------------------------------
#   technology-tagged (intens.)  log_collabs_battery         log_collabs_hydrogen
#   cross-border EU           log_collabs_eu_crossborder_battery  ..._hydrogen
#   cross-sector              log_collabs_crosssector_battery     ..._hydrogen
#   cross-sector (EU only)    log_collabs_crosssector_eu_battery  ..._hydrogen   [optional]
#   non-EU (placebo)          log_collabs_non_eu_battery          ..._hydrogen
#   domestic (placebo)        log_collabs_domestic_battery        ..._hydrogen
#   within-sector (placebo)   log_collabs_withinsector_battery    ..._hydrogen
#   cross-sector (NACE-1)     log_collabs_crosssector_nace1_battery  ..._hydrogen  [robustness]
#
outcome_map <- list(
  tech_focused = c(battery = "log_collabs_battery",
                   hydrogen = "log_collabs_hydrogen"),
  cross_border = c(battery = "log_collabs_eu_crossborder_battery",
                   hydrogen = "log_collabs_eu_crossborder_hydrogen"),
  cross_sector = c(battery = "log_collabs_crosssector_battery",
                   hydrogen = "log_collabs_crosssector_hydrogen"),
  cross_sector_eu = c(battery = "log_collabs_crosssector_eu_battery",
                      hydrogen = "log_collabs_crosssector_eu_hydrogen"),
  non_eu = c(battery = "log_collabs_non_eu_battery",
             hydrogen = "log_collabs_non_eu_hydrogen"),
  domestic = c(battery = "log_collabs_domestic_battery",
               hydrogen = "log_collabs_domestic_hydrogen"),
  within_sector = c(battery = "log_collabs_withinsector_battery",
                    hydrogen = "log_collabs_withinsector_hydrogen"),
  # Redirection benchmark: collaboration OUTSIDE the funded technology
  # (total minus technology-tagged, built in nb03).
  non_funded    = c(battery = "log_collabs_nonfunded_battery",
                    hydrogen = "log_collabs_nonfunded_hydrogen"),
  # Collaboration-level geography (built in nb03). The cross_border / non_eu /
  # domestic outcomes above are DYAD-level, so one collaboration can enter
  # several of them; these classify the collaboration as a whole from its
  # participants' headquarters countries and form two mutually exclusive pairs,
  # national vs cross-border and EU-internal vs international.
  cl_national      = c(battery = "log_collabs_national_battery",
                       hydrogen = "log_collabs_national_hydrogen"),
  cl_crossborder   = c(battery = "log_collabs_crossborder_battery",
                       hydrogen = "log_collabs_crossborder_hydrogen"),
  cl_eu_internal   = c(battery = "log_collabs_eu_internal_battery",
                       hydrogen = "log_collabs_eu_internal_hydrogen"),
  cl_international = c(battery = "log_collabs_international_battery",
                       hydrogen = "log_collabs_international_hydrogen"),
  # Sectoral distance at NACE-1, collaboration level and mutually exclusive.
  # Supersedes cross_sector / within_sector, which are dyad-level and overlap on
  # ~72% of the collaborations counted as within-sector.
  cl_crosssector_n1 = c(battery = "log_collabs_crosssector_n1_battery",
                        hydrogen = "log_collabs_crosssector_n1_hydrogen"),
  cl_samesector_n1  = c(battery = "log_collabs_samesector_n1_battery",
                        hydrogen = "log_collabs_samesector_n1_hydrogen"),
  # Robustness: cross-sector at NACE-1 resolution (nace2_proxy_nace1).
  # Same column auto-log-transformed by load_cs; primary cross_sector stays NACE-2.
  cross_sector_nace1 = c(battery = "log_collabs_crosssector_nace1_battery",
                         hydrogen = "log_collabs_crosssector_nace1_hydrogen")
)
```

```{r zero-shares}
# Zero shares among TREATED firm-periods (the binding constraint on power).
# Watch this when you flip to quarterly: it should drop noticeably.
zero_share_report <- function(df_b, df_h, map) {
  rows <- lapply(names(map), function(k) {
    cb <- sub("^log_collabs", "n_collabs", map[[k]]["battery"])
    ch <- sub("^log_collabs", "n_collabs", map[[k]]["hydrogen"])
    zb <- if (cb %in% names(df_b)) mean(df_b[df_b$is_treated == 1, cb] == 0) else NA
    zh <- if (ch %in% names(df_h)) mean(df_h[df_h$is_treated == 1, ch] == 0) else NA
    data.frame(outcome = k,
               battery_zero_pct  = round(100 * zb, 1),
               hydrogen_zero_pct = round(100 * zh, 1))
  })
  do.call(rbind, rows)
}
cat("\n--- Zero shares (treated firm-", TIME_UNIT, "s) ---\n", sep = "")
print(zero_share_report(battery_s1, hydrogen_s1, outcome_map), row.names = FALSE)
```

# 2. C&S Estimation --- Helper Functions

```{r cs-function}
run_cs <- function(df, yname, label = "",
                   # Was "notyettreated", which contradicted both cg_for() and
                   # the default in _cs_helpers.R. Every call site passes
                   # control_group explicitly, so this default never fired and
                   # aligning it changes no estimate; it removes the trap of a
                   # future call silently using the wrong comparison group.
                   control_group = "nevertreated",
                   clustervars   = NULL) {
  cat("\n=== C&S:", label, "(", yname, ") ===\n")
  if (!yname %in% names(df)) {
    cat("  !! column", yname, "not found -- skipping\n"); return(NULL)
  }
  # Deterministic per-outcome seed: makes every estimate reproducible and
  # independent of how many other outcomes ran earlier in the same session.
  # With a single set.seed() up front, adding one outcome shifts the bootstrap
  # stream for every later run and moves all downstream p-values.
  set.seed(42L + sum(utf8ToInt(paste0(yname, control_group))))
  cs_out <- att_gt(
    yname = yname, tname = "period", idname = "firm_id", gname = "g_period",
    control_group = control_group, clustervars = clustervars,
    anticipation = 0,   # paper assumption: treatment date = EC approval, no anticipation
    bstrap = TRUE, biters = BITERS, panel = TRUE, pl = TRUE, data = df
  )
  print(summary(cs_out))
  cs_out
}

agg_simple  <- function(cs) if (is.null(cs)) NULL else aggte(cs, type = "simple")
agg_dynamic <- function(cs) if (is.null(cs)) NULL else
  aggte(cs, type = "dynamic", min_e = -12, max_e = 24)

pval_from_att <- function(att, se) round(2 * pnorm(-abs(att / se)), 3)

sample_stats <- function(df, yname) {
  d <- df %>% filter(!is.na(.data[[yname]]), !is.na(firm_id),
                     !is.na(period), !is.na(g_period))
  data.frame(N_obs = nrow(d), N_units = n_distinct(d$firm_id),
             N_treated = n_distinct(d$firm_id[d$g_period > 0]))
}

# Pre-trend test. Primary is did's universal Wald pre-test (cs_out$Wpval). For
# staggered designs that bootstrap covariance is singular and att_gt returns no
# Wald (hydrogen, confirmed -- it stays NULL under never- AND not-yet-treated).
# In that case fall back to a joint test that the pre-period (e < 0) dynamic
# event-study coefficients are zero: a chi-square of their t-statistics from
# aggte(type="dynamic") att.egt/se.egt (analytic SEs, df = # pre-periods). The
# `method` field records which test was used.
es_pretrend <- function(cs_out) {
  if (is.null(cs_out)) return(list(stat = NA_real_, p = NA_real_, method = NA_character_))
  if (!is.null(cs_out$Wpval))
    return(list(stat = round(cs_out$W, 3), p = round(cs_out$Wpval, 3), method = "Wald"))
  dyn <- tryCatch(
    aggte(cs_out, type = "dynamic", min_e = -12, max_e = 24, bstrap = FALSE, cband = FALSE),
    error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(dyn)) return(list(stat = NA_real_, p = NA_real_, method = NA_character_))
  pre <- dyn$egt < 0
  t2  <- (dyn$att.egt[pre] / dyn$se.egt[pre])^2
  ok  <- is.finite(t2); k <- sum(ok)
  if (k == 0) return(list(stat = NA_real_, p = NA_real_, method = NA_character_))
  stat <- sum(t2[ok])
  list(stat = round(stat, 3), p = round(1 - pchisq(stat, df = k), 3), method = "ES-joint")
}

make_att_row <- function(agg_obj, technology, outcome, type = "Primary",
                         cs_out = NULL, df = NULL, yname = NULL) {
  if (is.null(agg_obj)) return(NULL)
  stats <- if (!is.null(df) && !is.null(yname)) sample_stats(df, yname) else
    data.frame(N_obs = NA, N_units = NA, N_treated = NA)
  pt <- es_pretrend(cs_out)
  data.frame(
    Technology = technology, Outcome = outcome, Type = type,
    TimeUnit   = TIME_UNIT,
    ATT = round(agg_obj$overall.att, 4),
    SE  = round(agg_obj$overall.se, 4),
    p_value = pval_from_att(agg_obj$overall.att, agg_obj$overall.se),
    pretrend_stat    = pt$stat,
    pretrend_p_value = pt$p,
    pretrend_test    = pt$method,
    N_obs = stats$N_obs, N_units = stats$N_units, N_treated = stats$N_treated,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}

plot_cs <- function(agg_dyn, title) {
  if (is.null(agg_dyn)) return(NULL)
  ggdid(agg_dyn, title = title) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = -0.5, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    labs(x = paste0(toupper(substring(TIME_UNIT, 1, 1)),
                    substring(TIME_UNIT, 2), "s relative to treatment"),
         y = "ATT(g,t)")
}

# Primary C&S control group: NEVER-TREATED for BOTH technologies. Some firms are
# treated in multiple IPCEI rounds, so a not-yet-treated firm may already be
# affected by an earlier treatment and contaminate the control pool; never-treated
# controls avoid this and make the two technologies symmetric. (Battery is a
# single cohort, which independently requires never-treated.) The not-yet-treated
# alternative is reported as one robustness row for hydrogen (section 6).
cg_for <- function(technology) "nevertreated"

# Convenience: run battery + hydrogen for one outcome key from outcome_map.
# Primary spec: never-treated controls + firm-level clustering, both technologies.
run_pair <- function(key, label) {
  list(
    battery  = run_cs(battery_s1,  outcome_map[[key]]["battery"],
                      paste("Battery S2 --", label),
                      control_group = cg_for("battery"),
                      clustervars   = "firm_id"),
    hydrogen = run_cs(hydrogen_s1, outcome_map[[key]]["hydrogen"],
                      paste("Hydrogen S2 --", label),
                      control_group = cg_for("hydrogen"),
                      clustervars   = "firm_id")
  )
}
```

# 3. Main Outcomes (technology-tagged)

```{r cs-tech}
cs_tech <- run_pair("tech_focused", "technology-tagged intensity")
cs_cb   <- run_pair("cross_border", "tech-tagged cross-border EU")
cs_xs   <- run_pair("cross_sector", "tech-tagged cross-sector")
cs_xs_n1 <- run_pair("cross_sector_nace1", "tech-tagged cross-sector (NACE-1 resolution)")
cs_neu  <- run_pair("non_eu",       "tech-tagged non-EU (placebo)")
cs_dom  <- run_pair("domestic",     "tech-tagged domestic (placebo)")
cs_ws   <- run_pair("within_sector","tech-tagged within-sector (placebo)")
cs_nf   <- run_pair("non_funded",   "collaboration outside funded technology")

# Collaboration-level geography: two mutually exclusive pairs. These replace the
# dyad-level cross-border EU / non-EU / domestic split as the sharper test of the
# scheme's geographic condition; the dyad-level outcomes are kept alongside.
cs_cln  <- run_pair("cl_national",      "collaboration-level national")
cs_clcb <- run_pair("cl_crossborder",   "collaboration-level cross-border")
cs_cleu <- run_pair("cl_eu_internal",   "collaboration-level EU-internal")
cs_clint<- run_pair("cl_international", "collaboration-level international")
cs_clxs <- run_pair("cl_crosssector_n1",  "collaboration-level cross-sector (NACE-1)")
cs_clss <- run_pair("cl_samesector_n1",   "collaboration-level same-sector (NACE-1)")

# Optional: cross-sector restricted to EU-EU ties. Comment out if not built.
cs_xseu <- tryCatch(run_pair("cross_sector_eu", "tech-tagged cross-sector (EU only)"),
                    error = function(e) list(battery = NULL, hydrogen = NULL))
```

# 4. Summary Table

```{r summary-table}
spec <- list(
  list(cs_tech, "Technology-tagged collaborations", "Primary", "tech_focused"),

  # The dyad-level geographic outcomes (cross_border / non_eu / domestic) are no
  # longer reported: a single collaboration could enter several of them at once,
  # so they double-count. They are superseded by the collaboration-level,
  # mutually exclusive set below. Still estimated above (cs_cb, cs_neu, cs_dom)
  # so the original specification stays reproducible, but kept out of att_table
  # and therefore out of the Benjamini-Hochberg family.

  list(cs_nf,   "Non-funded collaborations",         "Benchmark",  "non_funded"),

  list(cs_cln,  "National collaborations",          "Benchmark", "cl_national"),
  list(cs_clcb, "Cross-border collaborations",      "Primary",   "cl_crossborder"),
  list(cs_cleu, "EU-internal collaborations",       "Primary",   "cl_eu_internal"),
  list(cs_clint,"International collaborations",     "Benchmark", "cl_international"),
  list(cs_clxs, "Cross-sector collaborations",      "Primary",   "cl_crosssector_n1"),
  list(cs_clss, "Same-sector collaborations",       "Benchmark", "cl_samesector_n1")
)

att_table <- do.call(rbind, lapply(spec, function(s) {
  cs <- s[[1]]; outcome <- s[[2]]; type <- s[[3]]; key <- s[[4]]
  rbind(
    make_att_row(agg_simple(cs$battery), "Battery", outcome, type,
                 cs$battery, battery_s1, outcome_map[[key]]["battery"]),
    make_att_row(agg_simple(cs$hydrogen), "Hydrogen", outcome, type,
                 cs$hydrogen, hydrogen_s1, outcome_map[[key]]["hydrogen"])
  )
}))

cat("\n=== Tech-tagged ATT Summary (", TIME_UNIT, ") ===\n", sep = "")
print(att_table, row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(att_table,
          file.path(out_dir, "att_techtagged_table.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r export-event-studies}
# ============================================================
# Export tech-tagged dynamic ATT(e) in long format for notebook 08.
# The es_*.pdf files are ggdid's default style; 08 redraws in house
# style from THIS csv. One row per (technology, outcome, event_time).
# ============================================================

# (technology, outcome-label, cs object) for every outcome we want an ES for.
# Labels MUST match the convention notebook 08 filters on. Adjust the label
# strings here if 08 expects a different separator/spelling.
# Labels MUST match the Outcome strings in att_table, since notebook 08 filters
# the export on them. Geography and sector are the collaboration-level,
# mutually exclusive outcomes; the superseded dyad-level ones are not exported.
es_spec <- list(
  list("Battery",  "Technology-tagged collaborations", cs_tech$battery),
  list("Hydrogen", "Technology-tagged collaborations", cs_tech$hydrogen),
  list("Battery",  "EU-internal collaborations",       cs_cleu$battery),
  list("Hydrogen", "EU-internal collaborations",       cs_cleu$hydrogen),
  list("Battery",  "Cross-sector collaborations",      cs_clxs$battery),
  list("Hydrogen", "Cross-sector collaborations",      cs_clxs$hydrogen),
  list("Battery",  "Cross-border collaborations",      cs_clcb$battery),
  list("Hydrogen", "Cross-border collaborations",      cs_clcb$hydrogen),
  list("Battery",  "International collaborations",     cs_clint$battery),
  list("Hydrogen", "International collaborations",     cs_clint$hydrogen),
  list("Battery",  "National collaborations",          cs_cln$battery),
  list("Hydrogen", "National collaborations",          cs_cln$hydrogen),
  list("Battery",  "Same-sector collaborations",       cs_clss$battery),
  list("Hydrogen", "Same-sector collaborations",       cs_clss$hydrogen),
  list("Battery",  "Non-funded collaborations",        cs_nf$battery),
  list("Hydrogen", "Non-funded collaborations",        cs_nf$hydrogen)
)

# Consortium-size mechanism path: compute its C&S objects HERE so the dynamic
# event study is always exported. Section 10 (which writes consortium_size_att.csv)
# runs AFTER this chunk, so its cs_size does not yet exist on knit -- the old
# guard on exists("cs_size") silently dropped these rows. Estimator is IDENTICAL
# to Section 10: cg_for() control group, no clustering, so the ES matches the ATT.
# Event study uses the ACTIVE-month version (intensive margin), matching the
# headline mechanism in Section 10; falls back to the zero-filled column on old
# panels that predate 05a adding mean_collab_size_active.
SIZE_ES_COL <- if ("mean_collab_size_active" %in% names(battery_s1))
  "mean_collab_size_active" else "mean_collab_size"

if (RUN_CONSORTIUM && "mean_collab_size" %in% names(battery_s1)) {
  cs_size <- list(
    battery  = run_cs(battery_s1,  SIZE_ES_COL,
                      "Battery -- consortium size (mechanism)",
                      control_group = cg_for("battery")),
    hydrogen = run_cs(hydrogen_s1, SIZE_ES_COL,
                      "Hydrogen -- consortium size (mechanism)",
                      control_group = cg_for("hydrogen"))
  )
  es_spec <- c(es_spec, list(
    list("Battery",  "Consortium size (mean firms/collab)", cs_size$battery),
    list("Hydrogen", "Consortium size (mean firms/collab)", cs_size$hydrogen)
  ))
}

es_to_df <- function(tech, outcome, cs_obj) {
  if (is.null(cs_obj)) return(NULL)
  d <- tryCatch(agg_dynamic(cs_obj), error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(d)) return(NULL)
  # Simultaneous band: aggte() is called with cband = TRUE, so crit.val.egt is
  # the uniform critical value over the whole event-time path. Falls back to the
  # pointwise normal value only if the bootstrap did not return one.
  z <- if (!is.null(d$crit.val.egt) && is.finite(d$crit.val.egt))
    d$crit.val.egt else qnorm(0.975)
  data.frame(
    label      = paste(tech, "--", outcome),   # match 08's label convention
    Technology = tech,
    Outcome    = outcome,
    e          = d$egt,
    att        = d$att.egt,
    se         = d$se.egt,
    crit_val   = z,
    ci_lower   = d$att.egt - z * d$se.egt,
    ci_upper   = d$att.egt + z * d$se.egt,
    TimeUnit   = TIME_UNIT,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}

event_study_tt <- do.call(rbind, lapply(es_spec, function(s)
  es_to_df(s[[1]], s[[2]], s[[3]])))

write.csv(event_study_tt,
          file.path(out_dir, "event_study_techtagged.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
cat("\nWrote event_study_techtagged.csv:", nrow(event_study_tt), "rows,",
    length(unique(event_study_tt$label)), "outcome-technology series\n")
print(table(event_study_tt$label))
```

# 5. Extensive-margin robustness (binary outcome)

When a tech-tagged count is mostly zeros, a `log1p` ATT is dominated by the
zero mass and its magnitude is hard to read as an elasticity (Chen & Roth on
logs-with-zeros). A linear-probability C&S on the binary "any such tie this
period" outcome is an honest complement: the ATT is then a change in the
probability of forming that type of tie. Same identification, more
interpretable when events are rare.

```{r extensive-margin}
any_map <- lapply(outcome_map, function(v) sub("^log_collabs", "any_collabs", v))

# The three policy-targeted outcomes, i.e. the same family the Benjamini--
# Hochberg correction uses in section 8.
#
# Fixed Nov 2026. The old list was c("tech_focused", "cross_border",
# "cross_sector"); the last two name the DYAD-LEVEL outcomes, which Table 1
# stopped reporting in the collaboration-level rewrite, so "[ext] cross_sector"
# was the extensive margin of an outcome that appears nowhere in the paper.
# Selection is by KEY, never by display label: keys are stable identifiers,
# labels are what drifted and broke the Rosenbaum section. The label shown in
# the table is looked up from `spec`, so this table and Table 1 cannot disagree
# about what an outcome is called, and a missing key stops the run.
#
# Three keys, not the four Primary rows of `spec`: `agg_simple()` draws from the
# global RNG stream without reseeding, so changing the NUMBER of calls here
# would move every p-value in sections 6 and 7. Six calls in, six calls out.
ext_keys <- c("tech_focused", "cl_eu_internal", "cl_crosssector_n1")
ext_spec <- Filter(function(s) s[[4]] %in% ext_keys, spec)
if (length(ext_spec) != length(ext_keys))
  stop("Extensive margin: key(s) missing from spec: ",
       paste(setdiff(ext_keys, vapply(spec, `[[`, "", 4)), collapse = ", "))
ext_rows <- list()
for (s in ext_spec) {
  label <- s[[2]]; key <- s[[4]]
  cb <- run_cs(battery_s1,  any_map[[key]]["battery"],
               paste("Battery S1 -- EXT", key),
               control_group = cg_for("battery"))   # single cohort -> nevertreated
  ch <- run_cs(hydrogen_s1, any_map[[key]]["hydrogen"],
               paste("Hydrogen S1 -- EXT", key),
               control_group = cg_for("hydrogen"))
  ext_rows[[length(ext_rows) + 1]] <-
    make_att_row(agg_simple(cb), "Battery", paste0("[ext] ", label), "Ext. margin",
                 cb, battery_s1, any_map[[key]]["battery"])
  ext_rows[[length(ext_rows) + 1]] <-
    make_att_row(agg_simple(ch), "Hydrogen", paste0("[ext] ", label), "Ext. margin",
                 ch, hydrogen_s1, any_map[[key]]["hydrogen"])
}
ext_table <- do.call(rbind, ext_rows)
cat("\n=== Extensive-margin ATT (", TIME_UNIT, ") ===\n", sep = "")
print(ext_table, row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(ext_table,
          file.path(out_dir, "att_extensive_margin.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

# 6. Robustness (technology-tagged)

The primary spec (section 4) is the tighter-balance matched sample (`battery_s1`
= 1:3, `hydrogen_s1` = cal20_r2) with never-treated controls + firm-level
clustering. Robustness reuses `run_cs()` + `outcome_map`, the contiguous period
index and the firm-quarter aggregation (inheriting the `TIME_UNIT` toggle) and
reports two checks: (a) **larger control group** -- the SAME never-treated +
firm-clustered estimator re-run on the higher-ratio power matched sample
(`battery_s2` = 1:7, `hydrogen_s2` = cal15_r3); and (b)
**not-yet-treated controls** as one shown alternative (hydrogen only -- battery
is a single cohort with no not-yet-treated units), so the reader sees the primary
never-treated choice does not drive the results. The table is parallel to
section 4.

```{r robustness-techtagged}
# Outcomes to re-run -- mirrors the section-4 spec list (the optional
# cross_sector_eu outcome is skipped here).
# Mirrors the section-4 spec list: the collaboration-level, mutually exclusive
# geography and sector outcomes, not the superseded dyad-level ones.
rob_spec <- list(
  list("tech_focused",      "Technology-tagged collaborations"),
  list("cl_eu_internal",    "EU-internal collaborations"),
  list("cl_crosssector_n1", "Cross-sector collaborations"),
  list("cl_crossborder",    "Cross-border collaborations"),
  list("cl_international",  "International collaborations"),
  list("cl_national",       "National collaborations"),
  list("cl_samesector_n1",  "Same-sector collaborations"),
  list("non_funded",        "Non-funded collaborations")
)

# One robustness ATT row: pick the tech-tagged column from outcome_map, run C&S
# with the requested variant, return a section-4-parallel row (NULL-safe).
rob_one <- function(df, key, technology, outcome, variant,
                    control_group = NULL, clustervars = NULL) {
  # Default to the primary control group (never-treated, via cg_for). The
  # "Not-yet-treated controls" variant passes control_group explicitly to override.
  if (is.null(control_group)) control_group <- cg_for(technology)
  yn <- outcome_map[[key]][tolower(technology)]
  cs <- run_cs(df, yn,
               label         = paste(technology, "--", outcome, "--", variant),
               control_group = control_group,
               clustervars   = clustervars)
  make_att_row(agg_simple(cs), technology, outcome, variant, cs, df, yn)
}

rob_rows <- list()
for (s in rob_spec) {
  key <- s[[1]]; oc <- s[[2]]
  rob_rows <- c(rob_rows, list(
    # (a) larger control group (power spec, S2): SAME primary estimator
    #     (never-treated + firm clustering) on the higher-ratio matched sample
    rob_one(battery_s2,  key, "Battery",  oc, "Larger control group", clustervars = "firm_id"),
    rob_one(hydrogen_s2, key, "Hydrogen", oc, "Larger control group", clustervars = "firm_id"),
    # (b) not-yet-treated controls (hydrogen only; battery is a single cohort with
    #     no not-yet-treated units) -- shows the never-treated primary choice does
    #     not drive results
    rob_one(hydrogen_s1, key, "Hydrogen", oc, "Not-yet-treated controls",
            control_group = "notyettreated", clustervars = "firm_id")
  ))
}
rob_table <- do.call(rbind, rob_rows)

cat("\n=== Robustness checks (tech-tagged,", TIME_UNIT, ") ===\n", sep = "")
print(rob_table, row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(rob_table,
          file.path(out_dir, "robustness_techtagged_table.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

# 7. Rosenbaum Bounds (technology-tagged) --- RETIRED, `RUN_ROSENBAUM <- FALSE`

**This analysis is no longer reported and the code is kept for the record only.**
Matching is with replacement, so matched sets overlap: one battery and five
hydrogen controls sit in two matched sets at once, and the set independence that
`rbounds::psens` assumes fails. A valid matched-set procedure exists
(`sensitivitymult::senm`) but is not installed, and the pair contrast's estimand
(full pre-window baseline) differs from the C&S estimand (baseline at $g-1$),
which matters for hydrogen. The reasoning and the decision to drop the panel
from the appendix table are in `tables.py` around line 230.
`rosenbaum_bounds_techtagged.csv` is retained and marked obsolete rather than
deleted; its labels predate the collaboration-level rewrite, so do not quote it.
The selection bug described in the `rosenbaum-run` chunk was fixed in Nov 2026
so that a revival starts from working code, not so that this should be revived.

Method preserved exactly from the original file: collapse each matched set to a
post-treatment pair difference (treated firm vs the mean of its matched
controls, on `log1p` of the count) and run a Wilcoxon signed-rank sensitivity
analysis with `rbounds::psens` / `hlsens`. It reads the matched-firms and
cs_ready CSVs directly and works off the raw `month` / `g` dates, so it is a
matched-pair analysis unaffected by the period coding; only the tech-tagged
**count** columns (`n_collabs_*`, not the logs) are fed in. Outputs go to the
`TIME_UNIT` results folder.

```{r rosenbaum-function}
run_rosenbaum <- function(matched_firms_path, cs_panel_path,
                           outcome_col = "n_collabs_battery",
                           gamma_max   = 3.0,
                           gamma_inc   = 0.1,
                           label       = "") {

  cat("\n=== Rosenbaum Bounds:", label, "===\n")

  firms <- read.csv(matched_firms_path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  panel <- read.csv(cs_panel_path,      stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  panel$month <- as.Date(panel$month)

  g_lookup <- panel %>%
    filter(is_treated == 1) %>%
    distinct(Linkedin_name, matched_to, g) %>%
    rename(g_treated = g)

  panel_sym <- panel %>%
    left_join(
      g_lookup %>% select(matched_to, g_treated),
      by = "matched_to"
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      g_use  = ifelse(is_treated == 1, g, g_treated),
      g_date = as.Date(g_use),
      post   = !is.na(g_date) & month >= g_date
    ) %>%
    mutate(y = log1p(.data[[outcome_col]])) %>%
    group_by(Linkedin_name) %>%
    # DiD contrast, not a post-treatment level: each firm's own post-minus-pre
    # change. Pairing these changes makes the Rosenbaum null correspond to the
    # difference-in-differences estimand rather than to a level difference.
    summarise(y_mean = mean(y[post], na.rm = TRUE) - mean(y[!post], na.rm = TRUE),
              .groups = "drop") %>%
    filter(is.finite(y_mean))

  firms <- firms %>%
    left_join(panel_sym, by = "Linkedin_name")

  treated <- firms %>%
    filter(is_treated == 1) %>%
    select(matched_to, Linkedin_name, y_treated = y_mean) %>%
    rename(treated_name = Linkedin_name)

  controls_agg <- firms %>%
    filter(is_control == 1) %>%
    group_by(matched_to) %>%
    summarise(y_control = mean(y_mean, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

  pairs <- treated %>%
    left_join(controls_agg, by = "matched_to") %>%
    filter(!is.na(y_treated), !is.na(y_control))

  cat(sprintf("  Valid matched pairs: %d\n", nrow(pairs)))
  cat(sprintf("  Mean treated: %.3f | Mean control: %.3f\n",
              mean(pairs$y_treated), mean(pairs$y_control)))

  cat("\n-- Wilcoxon signed-rank sensitivity (psens) --\n")
  ps <- psens(pairs$y_treated, pairs$y_control,
              Gamma = gamma_max, GammaInc = gamma_inc)

  cat("\n-- Hodges-Lehmann sensitivity (hlsens) --\n")
  hl <- hlsens(pairs$y_treated, pairs$y_control,
               Gamma = gamma_max, GammaInc = gamma_inc)

  psens_df    <- as.data.frame(ps$bounds)
  gamma_break <- psens_df$Gamma[which(psens_df$`Lower Bound` > 0.05)[1]]

  cat(sprintf("\n  Lower bound p at Gamma=1: %.4f\n",
              psens_df$`Lower Bound`[1]))
  cat(sprintf("  Effect robust to hidden bias up to Gamma = %.1f\n",
              ifelse(is.na(gamma_break), gamma_max, gamma_break - gamma_inc)))

  invisible(list(psens = ps, hlsens = hl,
                 gamma_break = gamma_break, pairs = pairs))
}
```

```{r rosenbaum-run, eval=RUN_ROSENBAUM}
# Dynamic selection: test exactly the outcomes that are significant in THIS run,
# using the global SIG_THRESHOLD from the setup chunk.
#
# The label -> key lookup that used to live here has been DELETED (Nov 2026).
# It was hand-written, and five of its eight display labels were renamed in the
# collaboration-level rewrite ("Cross-border EU" -> "Cross-border", "Non-EU" ->
# "International", "Domestic" -> "National", "Within-sector" -> "Same-sector",
# and "Cross-sector EU-only" dropped entirely). Rows that failed to match were
# discarded by an !is.na() filter, silently, so a re-run would have tested three
# outcomes while appearing to test eight. Worse, "Cross-sector collaborations"
# DID still match, but onto key `cross_sector` -- the dyad-level NACE-2 outcome,
# not the collaboration-level NACE-1 `cl_crosssector_n1` that Table 1 reports --
# so the sectoral bound would have been computed on a different outcome from the
# ATT it exists to stress-test.
#
# This is the identical failure mode that section 9 had and that was fixed there
# by building the cell list from `spec`. Same fix here: `spec` is the single
# source of the (outcome label, key) pairing, so the two can no longer drift.
# Any rosenbaum_bounds_techtagged.csv written before this change carries the old
# labels and is void.
spec_keys <- do.call(rbind, lapply(spec, function(s)
  data.frame(Outcome = s[[2]], key = s[[4]], stringsAsFactors = FALSE)))

sig_rb <- att_table[!is.na(att_table$p_value) &
                      att_table$p_value < SIG_THRESHOLD, , drop = FALSE]
sig_rb <- merge(sig_rb, spec_keys, by = "Outcome", all.x = TRUE)

# A label in att_table with no key in spec is now an ERROR, not a silent drop:
# att_table is itself built from spec, so a mismatch means something upstream
# has been edited inconsistently and the run should stop rather than under-test.
if (any(is.na(sig_rb$key)))
  stop("Rosenbaum: no spec key for outcome(s): ",
       paste(unique(sig_rb$Outcome[is.na(sig_rb$key)]), collapse = ", "))

# Feed the tech-tagged COUNT column (n_collabs_*, not the log) for each
# significant (Technology, outcome) pair; matched-pair method unchanged.
if (nrow(sig_rb) == 0) {
  cat("No significant outcomes (p <", SIG_THRESHOLD,
      ") -- Rosenbaum bounds skipped.\n")
  rb_runs <- list()
} else {
  rb_runs <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(sig_rb)), function(i) {
    tech  <- sig_rb$Technology[i]
    is_b  <- tech == "Battery"
    fpath <- if (is_b) PATH_BATTERY_FIRMS_S1 else PATH_HYDROGEN_FIRMS_S1
    ppath <- if (is_b) PATH_BATTERY_S1       else PATH_HYDROGEN_S1
    ccol  <- sub("^log_collabs", "n_collabs",
                 outcome_map[[sig_rb$key[i]]][tolower(tech)])
    run_rosenbaum(fpath, ppath, outcome_col = ccol,
                  label = paste(tech, "--", sig_rb$Outcome[i]))
  })
  names(rb_runs) <- paste(sig_rb$Technology, "--", sig_rb$Outcome)
}
```

```{r rosenbaum-table, eval=RUN_ROSENBAUM}
if (length(rb_runs) == 0) {
  cat("Rosenbaum bounds table skipped (no significant outcomes).\n")
} else {
  make_rb_table <- function(rb_obj, label) {
    df <- as.data.frame(rb_obj$psens$bounds)
    df$Specification <- label
    df %>% select(Specification, everything())
  }

  rb_table <- bind_rows(Map(make_rb_table, rb_runs, names(rb_runs))) %>%
    filter(Gamma %in% c(1.0, 1.25, 1.5, 1.75, 2.0, 2.5, 3.0))

  cat("\n=== Rosenbaum bounds (tech-tagged,", TIME_UNIT, ") ===\n", sep = "")
  print(rb_table, row.names = FALSE)
  write.csv(rb_table,
            file.path(out_dir, "rosenbaum_bounds_techtagged.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
}
```

# 8. Benjamini--Hochberg Correction (technology-tagged)

BH applied **within each technology**, across the CONFIRMATORY outcomes only,
using the p-values from the section-4 `att_table`.

The confirmatory family is the three outcomes the scheme's conditions target,
as set out in the paper's outcome design: technology-related, EU-internal and
cross-sector collaboration. The benchmarks (total, technology-unrelated,
cross-border, international, national, within-sector) are reference quantities
rather than hypotheses the paper sets out to reject, so correcting across them
would control the false discovery rate over nulls that are not being tested.
The robustness operationalisations (NACE-1 and EU-only cross-sector) are
alternative measures of a confirmatory outcome, so including them would correct
the same hypothesis twice. Both are therefore excluded from the family and
reported with nominal p-values.

The correction across ALL estimated outcomes is still written to
`bh_correction_techtagged_alloutcomes.csv`. It is not reported in the paper;
it exists so the conservative figure is available if a referee asks.

```{r bh-correction}
bh_stars <- function(p) ifelse(is.na(p), "",
                        ifelse(p < 0.01, "***",
                        ifelse(p < 0.05, "**",
                        ifelse(p < 0.10, "*", ""))))

# Outcomes the scheme's conditions target. Defined by the paper's outcome
# design, not by the estimates.
CONFIRMATORY <- c("Technology-tagged collaborations",
                  "EU-internal collaborations",
                  "Cross-sector collaborations")

make_bh_df <- function(tech, outcomes = CONFIRMATORY) {
  sub   <- att_table[att_table$Technology == tech, ]
  if (!is.null(outcomes)) sub <- sub[sub$Outcome %in% outcomes, ]
  p_raw <- sub$p_value
  p_bh  <- p.adjust(p_raw, method = "BH")
  data.frame(
    technology = tech,
    outcome    = sub$Outcome,
    p_raw      = round(p_raw, 3),
    p_bh       = round(p_bh,  3),
    sig_raw    = bh_stars(p_raw),
    sig_bh     = bh_stars(p_bh),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}

bh_df <- rbind(make_bh_df("Battery"), make_bh_df("Hydrogen"))

cat("\n=== Benjamini-Hochberg, confirmatory family (", TIME_UNIT, ") ===\n", sep = "")
print(bh_df, row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(bh_df,
          file.path(out_dir, "bh_correction_techtagged.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# Not reported: the correction across every estimated outcome, kept available
# for a referee response.
bh_all <- rbind(make_bh_df("Battery", NULL), make_bh_df("Hydrogen", NULL))
cat("\n=== Benjamini-Hochberg, all outcomes (NOT REPORTED) ===\n", sep = "")
print(bh_all, row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(bh_all,
          file.path(out_dir, "bh_correction_techtagged_alloutcomes.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)
```

# 9. Power simulation (the insignificant outcomes)

Design-based power simulation on the REAL treated firms: the estimated effect
is subtracted from treated post-approval outcomes to impose the null, a
constant additive effect is then imposed on the log outcome over the
post-period, firms are resampled with replacement within cohort to generate
sampling variation, the C&S overall ATT is re-estimated per draw with the same
multiplier bootstrap as the reported estimates, and the rejection rate at the
5% level is recorded. The grid starts at zero, so every cell carries its own
size check. The earlier design drew synthetic treated firms from the matched
controls and overstated power in every cell; the full post-mortem is in the
`run_power_sim` header in `_cs_helpers.R`.

Four changes from the earlier version of this section:

1. **It runs on the insignificant outcomes, not the significant ones.** Power
   evidence is what distinguishes "no effect" from "cannot tell", so it is the
   *insignificant* estimates that need it; a significant estimate is its own
   proof of power. Section 3.4 of the paper already describes it that way. The
   candidate set is the full reported set (`spec`), and the only filter applied
   to it is `p >= POWER_SIG_THRESHOLD`, so nothing is included or excluded on
   the size of its own effect.
   *(Nov 2026: that filter is at 0.05, not the global 0.10, so the three
   outcomes between the two thresholds are covered. See `POWER_SIG_THRESHOLD`.)*
2. **The cell list is built from `spec`** (section 4), so it cannot drift from
   `att_table`. The previous version selected rows by p-value and then matched
   them on display labels; five of those labels were renamed in the
   collaboration-level rewrite, so those outcomes were silently skipped.
3. **The control group is passed in, not hard-coded.** The old inline copy ran
   `att_gt(control_group = "notyettreated")` while every reported estimate uses
   never-treated controls via `cg_for()`. Battery is a single cohort so the two
   coincide; staggered hydrogen is a different design.

The figure for the SI is drawn in notebook 08 from `power_all_outcomes.csv`;
the plot at the end of this section is a working check, not a paper exhibit.

```{r power-helpers}
# One definition of the power simulation, in _cs_helpers.R. Source it into its
# OWN environment and take only the power functions, so this script's inline
# run_cs / outcome_map / make_att_row are left untouched.
.power_env <- new.env()
sys.source("_cs_helpers.R", envir = .power_env)
run_power_sim  <- .power_env$run_power_sim
mde_at         <- .power_env$mde_at
POWER_PCT_GRID <- .power_env$POWER_PCT_GRID   # 5, 10, 15, 20, 30, 40 (%)
POWER_LOG_GRID <- .power_env$POWER_LOG_GRID   # the same grid in log points

# Draws per (technology, outcome, effect size). The Monte Carlo SE of a power
# estimate is at most 0.5/sqrt(n_sims): 3.5 points at 200 draws, 2.2 at 500.
# Simulating only the five null cells leaves room for 500, which matters because
# the number quoted in the text is where the curve crosses 0.80 and a 3-point
# wobble there moves the minimum detectable effect by a percentage point or two.
N_SIMS_POWER <- 500

# The null is imposed on the REAL treated firms (see the long note in
# _cs_helpers.R), so the effect grid gets a zero element: at a true effect of
# zero the rejection rate must come back near 0.05. That size check is the
# diagnostic that would have caught the previous placebo-from-controls design,
# so it runs with every cell rather than on request. `mde_at` is unaffected,
# since a point below 0.80 cannot move the first crossing.
POWER_GRID_RUN <- c(0, POWER_LOG_GRID)

# Multiplier-bootstrap draws INSIDE each simulated draw. The simulation has to
# mirror the inference the paper reports, and the reported SEs are bootstrap,
# not analytic: at battery's 29 clusters the analytic SE is ~1.7x too small, so
# the previous bstrap = FALSE version overstated power on its own. 9999 is
# unaffordable n_sims times over; 199 is enough for a reject/accept decision
# whose Monte Carlo error averages out across sims.
BITERS_SIM <- 199

# The effect sizes of a cell run in parallel, so one core per size keeps a
# cell to a single draw-batch of wall clock. Leave one core for the machine.
POWER_CORES <- max(1L, min(length(POWER_GRID_RUN),
                           parallel::detectCores() - 1L))

# Significance threshold for the POWER selection ONLY, deliberately not
# SIG_THRESHOLD. The global constant is 0.10 and also drives the Rosenbaum
# selection, so it must not move; but at 0.10 three outcomes that any referee
# working at 5% reads as nulls get no power curve -- battery national
# (p = 0.068), hydrogen international (0.055) and hydrogen cross-sector
# (0.083) -- while the SI caption and the results paragraph say "the
# non-significant outcomes" without qualification. Simulating at 0.05 makes
# that phrase true instead of something a reader can falsify from Table 1.
# Cost: 8 cells rather than 5. The `significant` column written to
# power_all_outcomes.csv uses THIS threshold, which is what notebook 08
# filters the SI figure on, so figure and caption agree by construction.
POWER_SIG_THRESHOLD <- 0.05
```

```{r power-cells}
# The power set IS the reported set.
power_cells <- do.call(rbind, lapply(spec, function(s)
  data.frame(Outcome = s[[2]], Type = s[[3]], key = s[[4]],
             stringsAsFactors = FALSE)))
power_cells <- merge(power_cells,
                     data.frame(Technology = c("Battery", "Hydrogen"),
                                stringsAsFactors = FALSE))
power_cells$yname <- mapply(function(k, tech) outcome_map[[k]][tolower(tech)],
                            power_cells$key, power_cells$Technology)
power_cells <- merge(
  power_cells,
  att_table[, c("Technology", "Outcome", "ATT", "p_value")],
  by = c("Technology", "Outcome"), all.x = TRUE)
power_cells$significant <- !is.na(power_cells$p_value) &
  power_cells$p_value < POWER_SIG_THRESHOLD
power_cells <- power_cells[order(power_cells$Technology, power_cells$Outcome), ]

# Only the nulls are simulated. A significant estimate is its own proof of
# power, so simulating it answers a question nobody asked and triples the
# runtime. The selection is on significance alone, applied to the full reported
# set, so no outcome is picked or dropped on the size of its own effect.
power_run <- power_cells[!power_cells$significant, ]

cat("\n=== Reported cells (", nrow(power_cells), "outcome x technology ) ===\n")
print(power_cells[, c("Technology", "Outcome", "yname", "ATT", "p_value",
                      "significant")], row.names = FALSE)
cat("\nSimulated (p >=", POWER_SIG_THRESHOLD, "):", nrow(power_run), "cells\n")
print(power_run[, c("Technology", "Outcome", "ATT", "p_value")],
      row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r power-timing, eval=RUN_POWER}
# Budget the run before starting it: time ONE draw per technology and
# extrapolate. Printed only.
for (tech in c("Battery", "Hydrogen")) {
  dfp <- if (tech == "Battery") battery_s1 else hydrogen_s1
  yn  <- outcome_map[["tech_focused"]][tolower(tech)]
  el  <- system.time(
    run_power_sim(dfp, yn, POWER_LOG_GRID[1], cg_for(tolower(tech)),
                  n_sims = 2, label = paste("timing", tech),
                  biters_sim = BITERS_SIM)
  )[["elapsed"]] / 2
  n_cells <- sum(power_run$Technology == tech)
  tot <- el * N_SIMS_POWER * length(POWER_GRID_RUN) * n_cells
  cat(sprintf("%-9s %.2f s/draw x %d sims x %d sizes x %d outcomes = %.1f h serial\n",
              tech, el, N_SIMS_POWER, length(POWER_GRID_RUN), n_cells, tot / 3600))
}
cat("Divide by mc.cores for the wall-clock estimate.\n")
```

```{r power-run, eval=RUN_POWER}
library(parallel)

# Robust parallelism: fork when available, fall back to serial if the fork
# workers fail (e.g. a non-interactive session), so an overnight run never
# silently returns no results.
mclapply <- function(X, FUN, ..., mc.cores = min(4L, parallel::detectCores())) {
  res <- tryCatch(parallel::mclapply(X, FUN, ..., mc.cores = mc.cores),
                  error = function(e) base::lapply(X, FUN))
  if (any(vapply(res, function(z) inherits(z, "try-error"), logical(1))))
    res <- base::lapply(X, FUN)
  res
}

power_rows <- list()
for (i in seq_len(nrow(power_run))) {
  tech <- power_run$Technology[i]
  dfp  <- if (tech == "Battery") battery_s1 else hydrogen_s1
  yn   <- power_run$yname[i]
  lbl  <- paste(tech, "--", power_run$Outcome[i])

  cat("Power simulation:", lbl, "(", yn, ")\n")
  # One core per effect size, so a cell costs one draw-batch of wall clock.
  # att_hat imposes the null: the estimated effect is removed from the treated
  # firms' post-periods before the hypothesised one is added, so the true effect
  # in a draw is `a` and not `a` on top of what the data already contain.
  grid_rows <- mclapply(POWER_GRID_RUN, function(a)
    run_power_sim(dfp, yn, a, cg_for(tolower(tech)),
                  n_sims = N_SIMS_POWER, label = lbl,
                  att_hat = power_run$ATT[i], biters_sim = BITERS_SIM),
    mc.cores = POWER_CORES)
  grid_rows <- grid_rows[!vapply(grid_rows, is.null, logical(1))]
  if (!length(grid_rows)) next

  out <- do.call(rbind, grid_rows)
  out$Technology  <- tech
  out$Outcome     <- power_run$Outcome[i]
  out$Type        <- power_run$Type[i]
  out$key         <- power_run$key[i]
  out$yname       <- yn
  out$ATT         <- power_run$ATT[i]
  out$p_value     <- power_run$p_value[i]
  out$significant <- power_run$significant[i]
  power_rows[[length(power_rows) + 1]] <- out
}

power_all <- do.call(rbind, power_rows)
power_all <- power_all[, c("Technology", "Outcome", "Type", "key", "yname",
                           "att_log", "att_pct", "power", "n_draws", "n_sims",
                           "ATT", "p_value", "significant")]
print(power_all, row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(power_all, file.path(out_dir, "power_all_outcomes.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)

# Any cell where draws failed to converge is a problem, not a rounding issue.
bad <- power_all[power_all$n_draws < power_all$n_sims, ]
if (nrow(bad)) {
  cat("\n!! draws that did not converge:\n"); print(bad, row.names = FALSE)
}
```

```{r power-mde, eval=RUN_POWER}
# Minimum detectable effect at 80% power, per cell. This is the number the
# robustness paragraph quotes for a null: "this sample detects effects of X% or
# larger in 80% of draws, so the null rules out effects above X%."
power_mde <- do.call(rbind, lapply(
  split(power_all, list(power_all$Technology, power_all$Outcome), drop = TRUE),
  function(d) data.frame(
    Technology  = d$Technology[1],
    Outcome     = d$Outcome[1],
    Type        = d$Type[1],
    ATT         = d$ATT[1],
    p_value     = d$p_value[1],
    significant = d$significant[1],
    mde_pct     = round(mde_at(d$att_pct, d$power, 0.80), 1),
    power_at_10 = d$power[which.min(abs(d$att_pct - 10))],
    power_at_20 = d$power[which.min(abs(d$att_pct - 20))],
    # Rejection rate when the true effect is zero. Must sit near 0.05; a value
    # far above it means the simulated population no longer matches the design
    # and the whole column is void. Read this BEFORE quoting any MDE.
    size        = d$power[which(abs(d$att_log) < 1e-12)[1]],
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)))
power_mde <- power_mde[order(power_mde$significant, power_mde$Technology,
                             power_mde$Outcome), ]
cat("\n=== Minimum detectable effect at 80% power ===\n")
cat("NA = the curve never reaches 80% over the grid tested.\n")
print(power_mde, row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(power_mde, file.path(out_dir, "power_mde_outcomes.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r power-plot-check, eval=RUN_POWER}
  if (nrow(pc)) {
```

# 10. Consortium size (mechanism check)

Did treated firms join LARGER multi-firm collaborations after approval? This is a
potential mechanical driver of the composition results. `mean_collab_size` is the
mean number of firms per collaboration a firm participates in, per period --- a
**level**, not a count and not a share. It is run on the RAW column: no `log1p`,
not in `outcome_map`. Control group via `cg_for()`, which is `nevertreated` for
both technologies (an earlier version of this line said hydrogen used
`notyettreated`; it does not, and has not since `cg_for()` was introduced ---
not-yet-treated appears only in the robustness panel in section 6);
`anticipation = 0` is already set inside `run_cs()`. `TIME_UNIT`-aware (quarterly averages the per-month means).

```{r consortium-size}
# Two versions, see the note above:
#   mean_collab_size_active -- NA in firm-months without a collaboration, so C&S
#     drops them and the ATT is INTENSIVE margin. This is the headline mechanism.
#   mean_collab_size        -- zero-filled, mixes extensive and intensive margins.
#     Reported alongside so the difference between the two is visible.
SIZE_COLS <- c(active = "mean_collab_size_active", allmonths = "mean_collab_size")
SIZE_LAB  <- c(active = "Consortium size (active months)",
               allmonths = "Consortium size (incl. zero-collaboration months)")

if (RUN_CONSORTIUM && "mean_collab_size" %in% names(battery_s1)) {
  cs_size <- list(); size_rows <- list()
  for (v in names(SIZE_COLS)) {
    col <- SIZE_COLS[[v]]
    if (!(col %in% names(battery_s1))) {
      cat("   ", col, "not in panel -- re-run 05a. Skipping.\n"); next
    }
    cs_size[[v]] <- list(
      battery  = run_cs(battery_s1,  col,
                        paste("Battery --", SIZE_LAB[[v]]),
                        control_group = cg_for("battery")),
      hydrogen = run_cs(hydrogen_s1, col,
                        paste("Hydrogen --", SIZE_LAB[[v]]),
                        control_group = cg_for("hydrogen"))
    )
    size_rows[[v]] <- do.call(rbind, list(
      make_att_row(agg_simple(cs_size[[v]]$battery),  "Battery",
                   SIZE_LAB[[v]], "Mechanism",
                   cs_size[[v]]$battery,  battery_s1,  col),
      make_att_row(agg_simple(cs_size[[v]]$hydrogen), "Hydrogen",
                   SIZE_LAB[[v]], "Mechanism",
                   cs_size[[v]]$hydrogen, hydrogen_s1, col)
    ))
  }
  size_table <- do.call(rbind, size_rows)
  # Back-compat: downstream code expects cs_size$battery / cs_size$hydrogen.
  cs_size <- if (!is.null(cs_size$active)) cs_size$active else cs_size$allmonths
  cat("\n=== Consortium size mechanism check (", TIME_UNIT, ") ===\n", sep = "")
  print(size_table, row.names = FALSE)
  write.csv(size_table,
            file.path(out_dir, "consortium_size_att.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
} else {
  cat("mean_collab_size not found in cs_ready panels --",
      "re-run notebook 05 to add it. Skipping mechanism check.\n")
}
```

# Notes for carrying this into your existing sections 5--10

Your downstream sections need only a **column-name swap** (and they inherit the
contiguous index + quarterly toggle for free, because they all reuse the
data frames and `run_cs()` defined above):

* **Robustness S1 / clustering / never-treated:** replace each `yname = "..."`
  with the tech-tagged column from `outcome_map`, e.g.
  `outcome_map$cross_border["hydrogen"]`.
* **Power simulation:** point `outcome_var` at the tech-tagged column; the
  zero share is higher, so expect the minimum detectable effect to rise --- this
  is exactly the quantity to report when justifying the quarterly check.
* **Rosenbaum bounds:** unchanged mechanics; just feed the tech-tagged count.
* **Export for Python:** dynamic exports use the corrected event-time index now,
  so your `08_ck_visualisation-results` event studies will be right at year
  boundaries.
